financial_summary: Auna SA is a small-cap healthcare business with a $340M market cap on $1.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +24% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $152M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.79× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 1.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.1% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
